proposals.entity_key: Past conditional for unconfirmed past information (journalistic)
value: Limited to journalistic reporting of information not confirmed by authorities
Not used for verified factual statements, where the indicative is required

evidence.notes: Derived from the conditionnel journalistique description and the trap about factual reporting.

proposals.entity_key: Past conditional with si clause in plus-que-parfait
value: The si clause must be in the plus-que-parfait; the past conditional never appears after si
Used only for hypothetical past situations that did not actually occur

evidence.notes: First entry is the stated condition and trap; the second follows from the hypothetical usage.

value: The auxiliary stays in the infinitive (avoir/être) and is never conjugated
Agreement with the subject occurs only when the auxiliary is être

evidence.notes: Both entries come from the rule's formation and its agreement note.

value: Applies only when the main clause is in a past tense such as the passé composé
Requires the direct speech to be in the future tense
Not applied when the main clause is in the present, which keeps the future form

evidence.notes: Derived from the stated conditions; the present-main-clause contrast is standard tense concordance.

proposals.entity_key: Past main clause: passé composé → plus-que-parfait
value: Applies only when the main clause is in a past tense such as the passé composé
Requires the direct speech to be in the passé composé
Not applied when the main clause is in the present, which keeps the passé composé

evidence.notes: Derived from the stated conditions; the present-main-clause contrast is standard tense concordance.

value: Applies only when the main clause is in a past tense such as the passé composé
Requires the direct speech to be in the present tense
Not applied when the main clause is in the present, which keeps the present form

evidence.notes: Derived from the stated conditions; the present-main-clause contrast is standard tense concordance.

proposals.entity_key: Past participle agreement with preceding direct object (que)
value: Limited to compound tenses where the direct object precedes the verb
Requires the relative pronoun que to refer back to that preceding direct object
No agreement occurs when the direct object follows the verb

evidence.notes: Built from the rule's conditions and agreement rule; the following-object restriction is the standard counterpart.

value: Limited to non-pronominal verbs conjugated with être
Does not apply to verbs conjugated with avoir unless a direct object precedes the participle
Pronominal verbs follow their own agreement rules instead

evidence.notes: First two entries follow from the rule's scope and conditions; the pronominal restriction is stated as the rule's exception.

value: Used only when one action precedes another
Agreement with the subject occurs only when the auxiliary is être
The auxiliary appears in the present participle (ayant/étant), never conjugated

evidence.notes: Derived from the rule's conditions, formation, and agreement note.

value: Does not apply to nouns already ending in -s, -x, or -z, which stay unchanged
Does not apply to nouns in -al, which form -aux
Does not apply to nouns in -eau or -eu, which take -x

evidence.notes: All three entries are the exceptions listed in the rule, expressed as limits on the -s rule.
